sentences.text: JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the accused has challenged the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 08.02.2016 passed in Special Case (POCSO) No.18/2015 on the file of Additional Sessions Judge,
Raichur ('the trial court' in brevity).
2.
The brief facts of the case are that, PW-1 is the victim in this case.

She is the daughter of PW-8.
PWs-1, 8 and the accused herein
are the residents of Harijanawada of Raichur Town.
They are the neighbours.

The accused for the first time between 01.07.2014 and 28.07.2014 took the victim to his house during night hours and had committed forceful sexual assault against her knowing fully well that she is a minor.
Again the accused took her to Chikkasugur village of Raichur Taluk 6-7 months prior to 05.01.2015, wrongfully confined her for a period of 3 days and forcibly committed sexual assault against her.

3. The victim escaped from the said place, due to differences with her mother, she goes to Bangalore,
she was rescued by Don Bosco Members and housed at Balamandir, Bangalore.
Medical examination of victim on 28.01.2015 revealed her 6 months' old pregnancy.
Thereafter she was sent to Raichur and housed at Balamandir, Raichur.
To the authorities of Balamandir at Raichur, the victim divulged the cause for her pregnancy and pointed towards the accused.

On her complaint,
Market Yard Police, Raichur, registered the case in Crime No.6/2015, the accused was arrested on 09.02.2015 and he was subjected to judicial custody.
PW-11/Vinod Guttedar, the CPI has conducted the investigation and filed the final report.
4. The accused is represented by his counsel.
The accused pleaded not guilty of the charge under Sections 366-A and 376 of IPC and Sections 4 and 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
The prosecution examined PWs-1 to 11 and marked Exs.P1 to P10.

During his examination, the accused denied the incriminating circumstances stating that there is a vacant land situated in front of his house, the mother of the victim made an attempt to grab it and there were frequent quarrels in this regard.
In order to grab the said land, he has been falsely implicated in this case.
No defence evidence was let in on behalf of the accused.
5. The trial court by the impugned judgment convicted the accused of the offences punishable under Sections 366-A and 376 of IPC and Sections 4 and 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Further imposed sentence of S.I. for 7 years and fine of Rs.15,000/- for the offence under Section 376 of IPC and in default of payment of fine, to undergo S.I. for three months.

S.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.5,000/-
for the offence under Section 366-A of IPC and in default of payment of fine, to undergo S.I. for one month.

The accused was further sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 7 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine, to undergo S.I. for three months.

Simple imprisonment for 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence under Section 12 of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine, to undergo S.I. for one months with all the sentences to run concurrently.
6. Aggrieved, the accused is before this court on the grounds that, there are material contradictions and omissions in the evidence, which is not appreciated in right perspective.

2 prosecution is inconsistent with the guilt of the accused and is consistent with his innocence.

sentences.text: The prosecution has not proved the charges beyond reasonable doubt, the impugned judgment is erroneous, illegal and calls for interference and sought for acquittal.

7. Heard the arguments of Sri.Shivashankar H.Manur, learned counsel for the appellant/accused and Sri.Sharanabasappa M.Patil, learned HCGP for the respondent/State and perused the records.
8.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the accused that there is no cordial relationship between the victim and her mother/PW-8. PW-8 after the death of her husband had an illicit relationship with the accused and for this reason, the accused was assisting PW-8, which was not liked by the victim and hence, the victim used to prosecute ill-will against the accused.

It is also contended that the victim is not innocent, she had a past instances of eloping with boys to Bangalore and she used to be brought back on several occasions, none of the said boys have been examined during the investigation nor brought before the court.

9. It is further contended that mechanical investigation is made with an intention to fix the accused,
inspite of child was born to the victim, DNA examination was not done to confirm whether the accused was the father of the child or not.
There is a suppression of evidence, the victim is not a trustworthy witness to be relied.
Except her testimony, there is no iota of evidence against the accused and these aspects have not been appreciated by the trial court and sought for interference of this Court.

10. Per contra, learned HCGP submitted that the accused is neighbour, had direct contact with the victim, for the reason of the victim going out of the village for one or two times, he took advantage of it and committed sexual assault against her.
The victim has directly pointed out that the accused was the person responsible for her pregnancy and child was also born to him.
Nothing has been demonstrated in the cross-examination as to why the evidence of victim cannot be relied upon.
There is no need for DNA profiling or any technical evidence when the victim herself points out the culprit, there is no requirement of corroboration for an act of this nature.

It is also submitted that the trial court has rightly appreciated the evidence, accepted the sole testimony of the victim in recording the conviction and it calls no interference, rather it has to be confirmed.

11. As regards imposing of sentence is concerned, learned HCGP contended that Section 4 of the POCSO Act mandates minimum sentence of 10 years whereas, the trial court has awarded 7 years of imprisonment and it needs to be enhanced.

12. In reply, learned counsel for the accused contended that Section 366A of IPC contemplates sentence which may extend to 10 years wherein the trial court has imposed full sentence against the accused which is against the principles of sentencing.
13. The prosecution though relied upon the evidence of PWs-1 to 11, the important witness to the case is PW-1, the victim, PW-8, the mother of the victim.

The other witnesses are formal witnesses,
such as, PW- 2/Shanthadevi, CDPO of Raichur, PW-3/Mustafa, panch witness to Exs.P2 and P3,
spot panchanama, who turned hostile, PW-4/Urukundappa is a panch witness to Ex.P2 and Ex.P3,

3 who knew nothing about the mahazar.

sentences.text: PW- 5/Hanumantha is a Constable, who carried FIR to the court.
PW-6/Ramachandra, Head Constable, who carried the material objects to FSL, Gulbarga.
PW- 7/K.Thippanna is a PDO of Grama Panchayat, Chikkasugur, who issued extract of Ex.P5 regarding place of incident.
PW-9/Pawankumar is a Revenue Officer, who issued Ex.P8/assessment extract of CMC, Raichur.
PW-10/Baby, PSI, who registered the FIR.

PW-11/Vinod Guttedar, the CPI,
who conducted the investigation.
14. Interestingly, the prosecution did not choose to examine the Medical Officer, who examined the victim either at Bangalore or at Raichur.
There is no FSL report available in favour of the prosecution and on record nothing is demonstrated that the DNA profile was conducted to ascertain the natural/biological parents of the child.
In this background, the only evidence that has been made available in favour of the prosecution is the victim alone.
15. The testimony of PW-2/Shanthadevi, the Superintendent of Balamandira, Raichur, goes to show that the victim was shifted from Bangalore to Raichur Balamandira.
At that time, the victim was six months' old pregnant.
She enquired with the victim how she became pregnant, to which victim disclosed the name of the accused leading to filing of complaint to the Police.
The cross-examination demonstrated that when the victim was shifted from Bangalore to Raichur, there are correspondences.
In these papers, name of the person, who is responsible for the pregnancy of the victim, found no place.
For the first time in Raichur, the name of the accused has been brought out and informed to the Police.

The evidence of this witness acquires importance for appreciating the evidence of PW-1.
16.
PW-3/Mustafa is a panch witness to the mahazar at Exs.P2 and 3 i.e., house of the accused and also house at Chikkasugur of Raichur.
His testimony shows that he attested Exs.P2 and P3 at the Raichur Police Station.
He was not taken either to the house of the accused or to Chikkasugur for drawing mahazar at Exs.P2 and P3.
He gives a clear go-by to the version of the prosecution.
Urukundappa is another panch witness to Exs.P2 and P3.
His testimony shows that one year prior to 20.01.2016, he was taken to Harijanawade where the Police have drawn Ex.P2/mahazar and he has attested to it.
8-10 days later, again he was called for mahazar where the accused shown Janata house at Yaramaras and the Police have drawn Ex.P3/mahazar.
PW-4 is not aware of the contents of either of the mahazars, so also the reason for the Police to draw up mahazar.
So it is clear that the Police have not taken him to Chikkasugur village for drawing Ex.P3/mahazar.
Hence, the place of inspection so proposed by the prosecution is not explained.
PW-4 says some mahazar was drawn at Harijanawade, for what reason is not known to him and he did not say anything about the mahazar drawn at Chikkasugur.

This is the quality of the evidence,
the prosecution expects the Court to accept it.
18. The testimony of PW-8, the mother of the victim shows that her husband has deserted her, she and the victim are residing together.
Her testimony also shows that the accused is her neighbour.
The victim used to visit the house of the accused frequently for doing some work.

She was not in the village for some time, when she came back, she came to know that her daughter has filed a complaint against the accused, she was not aware of the accused committing any forcible sexual Narashimhalu @ Bhabayya @ Babaloo vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48616091/
4 assault against the victim in his house or the accused repeating it by taking the victim to Chikkasugur.

sentences.text: She did not support the prosecution though in the cross- examination by the Prosecutor, nothing is elicited which will explain the version of the prosecution.
19. The cross-examination of PW-8 by the prosecution points out that the victim refused to stay with her mother, she had gone to Bangalore for studies and stayed in a hostel.
The cross-examination of PW-8 by the prosecution did not demonstrate anything in support of the prosecution as pleaded in this case.
She being the mother, she is not aware of the pregnancy of the daughter, delivery of the child.

A mother of this nature turning hostile towards the daughter shows the relationship and the concern to each other even though they were deserted by the husband of PW-8.
20.
The testimony of PW-11/Vinod Guttedar, CPI shows that mechanical investigation is carried out in this case.
He did not care to go for DNA profiling to ascertain whether the child belongs to the accused or not.

Because of the victim as well as the accused being poor, a shallow investigation is being done and mechanical drawing of the mahazar, arresting of the accused, subjecting him to custody and filing of the charge sheet done, this conduct of the Investigating Officer is deprecated.
The investigation of this nature certainly results in miscarriage of justice to the real victim.
Here is the Investigating Officer, who did not feel to get examined the Medical Officers, who examined the victim either at Bangalore or at Raichur.
No evidence is placed except marking the medical certificate as per Ex.P9 that the victim is pregnant.
As seen from the records, the victim going to Bangaluru along with 3 of her friends, they were not examined or there is no investigation done as required in a case of this nature.
The intention of Investigating Officer is so clear, a formal procedure to plant the predetermined culprit to the case.
21. The testimony of PW-1 shows that she stays with her mother, brother, grand-father and maternal uncle at Raichur.
Since her father has taken a second wife, he is residing separately.

About 1 years prior to 18.11.2015, the accused took her to his house, committed sexual assault and thereafter he took her to some other village, confined her for 3 days, he had repeatedly committed sexual assault against her.
She did manage to escape from the clutches of the accused, reached Bangalore through train where the people of Don Bosco Institute took her to Balamandira at Bangalore.
The people of Balamandira subjected her to medical examination where it was confirmed that she was four months' old pregnant.
She disclosed to them the name of the accused as the person responsible for her pregnancy.
2 months thereafter she was shifted to Balamandira, Raichur, where she files a complaint under Ex.P1.
She has also taken the Police and shown the place.
She gave birth to a male child, which was given in adoption, by the Balamandira people.
22. The cross-examination of PW-1 demonstrated that when she was 14 years old, she was escaped from her village, gone to Bangalore, stayed in Don Bosco Institute for two months.
She gives reason for her to leave the village was that her mother used to beat her, she was not tolerating the pinpricks of her mother and does not want to stay with mother.

She also tells that, along with one Govinda,
Channu and Anjali, she went to Bangalore.

In the Cross examination it was suggested to her that the accused and her mother were in cordial relationship, they are roaming together and they were moving outside village was not liked by her, she has denied these aspects, the manner in which her mother has given evidence supports the said aspect.

sentences.text: It is seen from the cross-examination that the house of the accused is in the neighbourhood of 30-40 houses.
Inspite of the accused committing sexual assault against her, she did not divulge to her mother, grand-father, maternal uncle, brother or her neighbours.
When she was examined at Bangalore, she was four months' old pregnant, she did reveal the name of the accused to the people of Don Bosco, but there was no complaint filed at Bangalore.
Rather, it is found from the evidence of PW-2 that when the victim was brought to Raichur Balamandir, she was six months' pregnant.

The history of pregnancy was not divulged in any of the papers, which shows that for a period of two months, there was no complaint filed at Bangalore, only after keeping the victim for two months at Bangalore, she was shifted to Raichur.

It shows that the officials of Balamandira, Bangalore, as well as the Medical Officer, who examined her at Jayanagar General Hospital, knew that the accused was the culprit, but it was not brought to the knowledge of the World.
For this lacuna, nothing is found as an explanation why it was suppressed.
As seen from the evidence of PW-2, the victim was six months pregnant when brought to Raichur Balamandira and thereafter the complaint came to be filed.

24. The cross-examination of the victim demonstrates that she was in the habit of leaving the village frequently, going to Bangalore and ultimately when she was found pregnant, she points out towards the accused.

Interestingly, the Investigating Officer did not examine the friends of victim viz.,
Govinda, Channu and Anjali with whom the victim had gone to Bangalore.
As regards the conduct of the victim, she is not an innocent child of village.
She knew how to escape from the village, visited Bangalore several times, stayed at Don Bosco Institute regularly and she being stayed in Balamandira, Bangalore.

Complaint says though she was subjected to medical examination inspite of knowing the accused was responsible, she did not divulge the name of accused, only after shifting to Raichur, for the first time, she divulged the name of the accused.
Her evidence is total contrary to it.
This explains that the victim is not a trustworthy witness for acceptance.

25. No doubt, as pointed out by the learned HCGP that in a case of this nature, the self-serving testimony of the victim is suffice to convict the accused, but such self-serving testimony is found to be trustworthy, unblemished, cogent and truthful and shall inspire the confidence of the court.

26. It is pertinent to note that there is no medical evidence, which points out that the accused was the father of the child, which gave birth by the victim, unless the DNA profile explains that the accused was the natural/biological father of the child, I do not find any reason to say that the testimony of the victim is reasonable for acceptance.

27. The victim is not aware of the name of the village where the accused confined her, panch witness did not point out the accused taking the Police and the panch witness to Chikkasugur village where the place was shown as the place of alleged incident.
There is no proper spot inspection conducted by the Investigating Officer and mechanically papers have been prepared and charge sheet has been filed.
28. I have carefully perused the impugned judgment and also the reasonings recorded by the trial court.
It is very unfortunate that the trial court did not discuss anything the aspect of delay in divulging the name of the accused.

If the evidence of the victim is to be appreciated that she has Narashimhalu @ Bhabayya @ Babaloo vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48616091/
6 informed the Don Bosco people as well as the Balamandira at Bangalore, why they have not taken any action to inform the Police.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Only after two months, she was shifted out of Bangalore and for the first time, the victim reveals the name of the accused to PW-2 and then the prosecution started.
Inspite of the accused committing act of sexual assault she did not inform it to her mother, grand parents, uncle or brother.
In spite of she was found missing from the village for 8 months, there was no missing complaint filed to the police.

Prosecution though claims kidnapping by the accused,
there is no iota of evidence which speaks that the accused induced the victim to accompany, much apart she claims accompanying the accused to other village.

The reason can be inferred that for the reason of escaping from village in a routine act of the victim, her mother and relatives did not choose to make any attempt to search for her whereabouts or to inform the police to help them to trace her out.
As it was regular for them to bring her from Bangaluru to village, they ignored her.
The mechanical investigation without applying mind did point out that sole testimony of PW-1 is not trustworthy.
Hence, placing reliance on the self- serving testimony of the victim is dangerous in her background and the weight of the evidence placed before the court.
29. Since the case has been filed under the provisions of POCSO Act, the trial court without appreciating the evidence in a proper perspective, mechanically passed the impugned judgment.

30. It is seen from the impugned judgment, the manner of sentencing of 7 years of imprisonment for Section 4 of POCSO Act against minimum sentence of 10 years and also for offence under Section 366A of IPC, though the sentence is upto 10 years but maximum sentence awarded points out non-application of mind by the trial court not only in appreciating the evidence, but also in sentencing.
Thus, it is a fit case where total miscarriage of justice has happened not only to the victim but also to the accused.
Therefore, I do not find any quality in the prosecution evidence for its acceptance and to ratify the impugned judgment.

31. Above all, I see that the accused is in incarceration at the time of investigation for a period of four months 27 days and post-conviction, he is in incarceration for 5 years 11 months 19 days, in all,
6 years 4 months 16 days, which, in the facts and circumstances of the case, even otherwise taken into consideration, is a sufficient sentence for the allegations made against the accused.
Hence, the accused cannot be continued in incarceration at the public cost and he deserves to be acquitted.
32. In the result, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I pass the following order:
The appeal is allowed.

Consequently, the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 08.02.2016 passed in Special Case (POCSO) No.18/2015 on the file of Additional Sessions Judge,
Raichur, is hereby set aside.
The appellant/accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 366-A and 376 of IPC and Sections 4 and 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
